name: The AI Enablement Audit
title: The AI Enablement Audit
answer: The AI Enablement Audit is a structured review of an organization's readiness to deploy AI systems safely and lawfully. It covers the inventory of AI models and tools in use, the data they touch, the business processes they support, and the controls around access, logging, and change management. The audit also maps each system to applicable internal policies, contractual obligations, and regulatory requirements, including intellectual property exposure and pending litigation risk. It is not a technical penetration test alone; it is a cross-functional check of people, process, and technology.

AI Security Audits and Enterprise Enablement

sections.body: The AI Enablement Audit is a structured review of an organization's readiness to deploy AI systems safely and lawfully. It covers the inventory of AI models and tools in use, the data they touch, the business processes they support, and the controls around access, logging, and change management. The audit also maps each system to applicable internal policies, contractual obligations, and regulatory requirements, including intellectual property exposure and pending litigation risk. It is not a technical penetration test alone; it is a cross-functional check of people, process, and technology.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The audit runs on the organization's existing governance, risk, and compliance stack, plus lightweight discovery tooling. It typically draws on identity and access management logs, data catalogs, model registries, code repositories, and vendor management records. Where AI is delivered through cloud APIs or embedded software, the audit reviews service agreements, data residency, and the boundary between first-party and third-party responsibility. No new hardware is required; the work is mostly document review, interviews, and configuration checks.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done in three passes. First, an inventory pass identifies every AI system, model, prompt template, and data pipeline in scope, including shadow deployments found through expense, procurement, and network logs. Second, a control pass tests whether each system has documented ownership, a lawful basis for data use, human review where required, and an incident response path. Third, a risk pass scores findings by likelihood and impact, separating blockers from improvements, and produces a remediation backlog tied to named owners and dates.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk are treated as a single thread. The audit checks whether training data, fine-tuning data, and outputs respect copyright, trade secret, and contractual restrictions, and whether the organization can show provenance for each model and dataset. It also reviews privacy notices, data protection impact assessments, and the handling of personal data in prompts and logs. Because the legal environment is moving quickly, the audit references the site's tracked active AI lawsuits, case law precedents, and state AI bills only as an external risk register, not as a compliance checklist. The output is a set of findings with severity, ownership, and evidence, not a pass or fail certificate.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The AI Enablement Audit is moving from a one-time project to a continuous control. Organizations are beginning to run lightweight enablement checks at each model release, vendor renewal, and material data change, rather than waiting for an annual review. The next stage ties audit findings to automated policy checks in the model deployment pipeline, so that a model cannot ship without evidence of data provenance, access control, and human oversight. Over time, the audit is expected to merge with existing third-party risk and software supply chain reviews, treating AI models as another governed asset class.
